papers.title_en: Temporal Specification Guidance for Text-to-Video Generation
papers.authors: Avishree Khare, Hideki Okamoto, Bardh Hoxha, Georgios Fainekos, Rajeev Alur
papers.evidence: 基于时序规范的可控文本到视频生成
papers.tldr: 文本到视频模型常能生成提示中的视觉概念，却难满足顺序、时序与持续时长要求。作者将要求形式化为时序逻辑规范，提出免训练推理期框架TSG，把规范转为可执行采样目标；它用可微定量语义给概念证据轨迹打分，以梯度构造引导去噪方向，并借助视频-文本注意力轨迹、MTL可微分数与梯度注意力偏置实现，无需外部分类器或反传视频Transformer。在220条、11类时序约束基准上，TSG相较CFG将规范满足准确率提升9.5至20个百分点，显存开销很小。
papers.abstract_en: Text-to-video models often generate the visual concepts requested in natural language prompts but fail to satisfy their intended ordering, timing, and persistence requirements. We propose representing these requirements as specifications in a formal Temporal Logic, and introduce Temporal Specification Guidance (TSG), a training-free inference-time framework that turns temporal specifications into executable objectives for guiding video generation during sampling. TSG scores traces of visual concept evidence using differentiable quantitative semantics and uses the score's gradients to construct a specification-guided denoising direction. We instantiate this framework with video-text attention traces, efficient differentiable scores for Metric Temporal Logic, and gradient-derived attention biases. This instantiation requires neither an external concept classifier nor backpropagation through the video transformer. Its attention-steered forward pass yields a denoising direction that augments classifier-free guidance (CFG). On a benchmark of 220 prompts spanning 11 categories of temporal constraints, including ordered object entry and state transitions, this instantiation improves specification satisfaction accuracy over CFG by 9.5-20 percentage points across five models, with minimal memory overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of temporal specifications and differentiable satisfaction objectives as a flexible interface for controlling video generation.

papers.title_en: Map2Vid: Embodied Navigation Video Generation with Human-Friendly Motion Control
papers.authors: Yulin Dai, Yuqian Fu, Tianwen Qian, Zhen Xing, Bojia Zi, Xiaoling Wang
papers.evidence: 通过鸟瞰图控制实现可控具身导航视频生成
papers.tldr: 现有可控视频生成虽视觉质量出色，但文本提示空间歧义、相机轨迹控制低层且不直观，难以服务具身导航。为此，作者提出Map2Vid任务，把导航视频生成重构为BEV地图到视频的合成，并构建覆盖61个室内场景、逾10万条序列的大规模基准。方法以统一框架融合多控制信号，并用课程训练逐步弱化非地图输入，支持完整条件与仅地图输入推理。多类基础生成模型实验表明该路线可行且有前景，为人类友好的导航视频生成提供了新范式。
papers.abstract_en: Controllable video generation has recently achieved impressive visual quality, yet existing control paradigms remain poorly suited to embodied navigation. Text prompts are spatially ambiguous, while camera-trajectory control relies on low-level motion specifications that are unintuitive for human users and difficult to manipulate. In this work, we introduce Map2Vid, a novel task that reformulates embodied navigation video generation as a BEV-map-to-video synthesis problem, together with a large-scale benchmark for systematic evaluation. By using BEV maps, which provide a visual representation of global scene layout and intended navigation routes, Map2Vid enables human-friendly navigation video generation. To support this task, we construct a dedicated dataset with over 100K navigation sequences across 61 indoor scenes, each paired with egocentric videos, BEV maps, camera trajectories and language instructions. We further develop a unified framework that integrates multiple control signals, together with a curriculum training strategy that progressively weakens non-map inputs, enabling flexible inference under both full conditioning and map-only input. Extensive experiments across multiple foundation generation models demonstrate that controllable navigation video generation via BEV map is a viable and promising direction.

papers.title_en: GeoART: Geometry-Aware Refinement via Test-Time Scaling for Camera-Conditioned Video Diffusion
papers.evidence: 相机条件视频扩散结合几何感知精修提升相机可控性
papers.tldr: 相机条件视频扩散模型常因去噪中相机约束与估计几何约束弱，导致相机控制不准和几何不一致。GeoART 提出免训练几何感知测试时缩放自精炼框架，在选定去噪步通过 Predict-and-Perturb 生成候选并用几何先验评估，经置信门控和排序校准概率选择推进状态。实验在相机可控性、多视角一致性和视觉质量上稳定优于现有采样与自精炼方法，且无需训练或改动预训练模型。
papers.abstract_en: Camera-conditioned video diffusion models often suffer from inaccurate camera control and geometric inconsisten- cies because camera constraints and estimated geometry are only weakly enforced during denoising. Existing reme- dies often require costly geometry-aware fine-tuning or ad- ditional 3D supervision. We introduce GeoART, a training- free self-refinement framework that improves camera con- trollability through geometry-aware test-time scaling. At selected denoising steps, GeoART generates multiple can- didates within the Predict-and-Perturb cycle and eval- uates them using a geometry prior, without directly modify- ing the denoising trajectory. A confidence gate suppresses unreliable geometric evidence, while rank-calibrated prob- abilistic selection combines score magnitude and relative rank to choose the next refinement state. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in camera controlla- bility, multi-view consistency, and visual quality over exist- ing sampling and self-refinement methods, without training or modifying the pretrained video diffusion model

papers.title_en: UniState: Unifying Memory and Intervention for Controllable World Simulation
papers.authors: Jaeseok Jeong, Kyungmook Choi, Sohyun Chung, Youngsik Yun, Youngjung Uh
papers.evidence: 统一空间记忆与用户干预的可控世界模拟
papers.tldr: 世界模型虽能提供丰富探索环境，但自由视角下干预并观察后果仍困难。UniState用统一世界状态表示结合空间记忆与用户干预，让用户直接在记忆中指定物体运动并独立选择相机轨迹。实验表明其联合物体与相机控制优于现有方法，且干预引发的场景变化可在多次 rollout 中保持。该框架消除了运动与视角控制的歧义，并保留模型合成额外合理运动的能力。
papers.abstract_en: World models offer increasingly rich environments for exploration, yet intervening in a world while observing the consequences from freely chosen viewpoints remains challenging. We tackle these challenges by introducing UniState, a framework for controllable world simulation built on a unified world-state representation. This representation unifies spatial memory and user interventions. Users specify object motion directly within spatial memory, while independently choosing the camera trajectory from which the resulting world state is observed. This unification makes the relationship between the scene and the requested changes explicit, removing ambiguity between object motion and viewpoint change from the control specification. Crucially, specifying an intervention does not require prescribing every resulting movement: the video model can synthesize additional motion within controlled objects and plausible interactions with their surroundings. We develop training and sampling strategies that help generated videos follow the specified object motion and camera trajectory while preserving this capacity to generate responses beyond the prescribed transformations. Experiments demonstrate more accurate joint object and camera control than the existing methods, alongside qualitative evidence that intervention-induced scene changes persist across rollouts.
